transcript.content: Hello, welcome to the clinic. What brings you in to see me today?

I guess… I’ve just been feeling really weighed down. Like I’m on edge most of the day, waiting for something else to go wrong. And I keep blaming myself for not stopping what happened. It’s been hard to shake.
Have you been feeling sad most of the time?

Yeah… I guess not sad exactly all the time, but there’s this heavy feeling that doesn’t really let up. Mostly fear and guilt. Like I’m bracing for something bad, and I keep thinking I should’ve stopped it somehow.
Do you often find yourself worrying about everyday things?
Not everyday things, exactly. It’s more like… this constant worry that something bad is going to happen again. I stay tense, and I keep going over how I should’ve stopped it.
Have you been avoiding certain places, people, or activities because of what happened?

Yeah… some. I’ve been turning down certain jobs, like if there’s a raised porch or a second-story deck involved. And at home I’ll… I’ll find reasons not to talk about the repair, or look over at the spot where it happened.
Are there any other activities or situations you've been avoiding because they remind you of what happened?

Mostly the same kinds of things… I avoid jobs if they involve raised porches or second-story decks. And at home, I’ll kind of dodge conversations about fixing it, or I just don’t look over at that spot if I can help it.
Do you ever find yourself reliving the moment when it happened, like it's happening all over again?

Yeah… sometimes. It’ll hit me out of nowhere, like if I’m measuring a railing or hear a ladder scrape. I can see him falling again, like it’s right there, and my stomach just drops… my hands get shaky.
Do you ever feel like you're outside of your body watching yourself when you're reliving the moment when it happened?
I don’t think so… not like I’m watching myself from outside. It’s more just… I’m back in it for a second, if that makes sense.
Do you ever feel numb or disconnected from the world around you?
I don’t know… not really, I guess. I haven’t noticed feeling numb like that. Sometimes I get quiet, but I’m still aware of what’s going on.
Do you ever have vivid memories or images of what happened that feel very real, like you're reliving it?

Yeah… I mean, I guess so. It’s not all the time, but if I’m measuring a railing or I hear a ladder scrape, it can just come up. I can see him falling like it’s right in front of me, and my stomach drops… my hands get shaky.
Do you try to avoid thinking about what happened?
Yeah… I guess I do. I’ve been turning down jobs if they involve raised porches or second-story decks. And at home I kind of… avoid talking about the repair, or looking over at where it happened.
Has what happened been affecting your relationships or work in any significant way?

A little, yeah. I’m still working, but it’s… slower. My reports take longer because I keep second-guessing what I wrote or measured. And I’ve been saying no to elevated deck or porch jobs, which I didn’t used to think twice about.
How long have you been feeling this way since what happened?
About four months now… since my husband fell during the porch repair.
Have you noticed any significant changes in your ability to interact with friends and family since the accident?

Not so much with friends and family, I guess… at least not in a big obvious way. It’s more shown up with work. I’m still doing inspections, but my reports take longer because I keep second-guessing them, and I’ve been turning down elevated deck or porch jobs I used to just take.
Do you find yourself trying not to think about your husband's fall or the porch repair?
Yeah… I do. I’ve been turning down jobs with raised porches or second-story decks. And at home I kind of… find reasons not to talk about the repair, or even look at the spot where it happened.
Have you been avoiding other things or situations besides jobs with raised porches or second-story decks and conversations about the repair at home?
Not really anything else I can think of. It’s mostly those porch or deck jobs… and at home, I just try not to bring up the repair or look over at that spot.
Have you lost interest in activities you used to enjoy?
I don’t think so… not in any clear way. I still do the things I usually do, I guess. Nothing really stands out there.
Have you noticed yourself pulling back from or losing interest in things you normally find enjoyable since your husband's accident?
No… I don’t think so. I mean, I’m not really pulling back from the usual stuff, at least not that I’ve noticed.
Have you felt less interested in hobbies or activities that were important to you since your husband's accident?
No… I can’t really say that I have. I still do the things I usually do. Nothing important comes to mind.
